tasks.instruction: Write a discussion response. An effective response contains at least 100 words.

professor.name: Doctor Diaz
professor.text: Some educators think that in our global, tech-oriented world, students need to focus on nonfiction texts, such as news stories, technical manuals, or other informational materials. They say that reading poetry, novels, and short stories is not the optimal use of the limited time that students have in the classroom. How do you view this approach of education? Should schools limit the teaching of fictional texts in favor of teaching more practical, nonfiction texts?

posts.name: Andrew
posts.text: Education has to evolve. Nowadays, there's an enormous amount of economic and political data freely available online. It's important that students can evaluate this information to understand local and world events in order to be good citizens. Reading fiction is a wonderful hobby, but school should prepare students for adult life and its responsibilities.

posts.name: Claire
posts.text: I spent a lot of class time in high school analyzing literature. I'm studying to be an engineer, so I admit that reading fiction in school was not directly applicable to my future occupation, but it did instill in me a love of reading, which is very valuable. I feel better equipped now to understand all sorts of written material.

tasks.sample:
From my perspective, the ability to read and write fictional texts is crucial to students, and schools should not limit the teaching of it.

To begin with, students can have richer social experiences with education in fictional texts. It is very common that people make friends based on shared interests, and education in fictional texts guides students into the world of stories and romances, allowing them to make friends with people who have similar tastes. There are fan clubs of all kinds of books, such as the Harry Potter or Game of Thrones franchise, where students can develop friendships, while non-fiction texts hardly serve this purpose.

More importantly, teaching fictional texts provides students with more career options. Today’s world is not only about science and technology, but also about cultures and arts. Students pursuing a career in businesses such as the movie industry or the advertising industry would need a formal school education to acquire the skills demanded in these fields. For example, without creative writing skills, someone cannot be a successful Hollywood playwright.

In conclusion, schools should keep teaching fictional texts.
